critic_risk_flags: Compared with the 2-week delay options and the series’ existing discovered pattern, a fixed 1-week delay is more likely to introduce phase error for hospitalization-rate targets (often lagging infection proxies). With sharp peaks, mis-specified delay can dominate fit/forecast timing; keeping both fractional memory and SEIRS further compounds flexibility.

I+H observation is poorly aligned to a hospitalization-rate target unless there is a clear measurement rationale; it risks conflating infection prevalence with admissions/census and inflating baseline. With an explicit H compartment already weakly identifiable in short series, adding a mixed observation map increases non-identifiability and interpretability issues.
